chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with them) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said in a long narration:
The month of Ramadan is thirty days, as the Honorable, the Exalted God says: 'And to complete the prescribed period...' and 'complete' means the full/thirty days.

key_terms.وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ: And to complete the prescribed period (Quranic quote)

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic evidence for Ramadan being thirty days according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking the fixed thirty-day duration of Ramadan to the Quranic phrase 'to complete the count' (2:185), interpreting 'complete' as denoting a full, unbroken month. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the precise calculation of lunar months for worship, reinforcing the authority of the Imams in deriving legal rulings from the Quranic text.
